database_summary: This is a small event/club finance and membership database (SQLite) containing tables for events, members, majors, zip codes, attendance (bridge), budgets, expenses, and income. The schema mixes descriptive/reference tables (major, zip_code), entity/state tables (event, member, budget) and transactional/event tables (attendance, expense, income). Foreign keys link attendance -> event/member, budget -> event, expense -> member/budget, income -> member, and member -> major/zip_code. Typical usage: report attendance by event/member, roll up budgets/expenses/income by event or category, join member demographic attributes (major/zip) to financial or attendance data. Some joins can multiply rows (attendance, expense, income) when aggregated without care.

accepted.name: event_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  event_name,
  event_date,
  type,
  notes,
  location,
  status,
  -- attempt to coerce ISO-like datetimes to a sortable numeric epoch (seconds since 1970). If parse fails, NULL
  CASE
    WHEN event_date IS NULL OR trim(event_date) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE (strftime('%s', substr(event_date,1,19)))
  END AS event_epoch,
  -- date-only portion (YYYY-MM-DD) when event_date contains an ISO datetime or date
  CASE
    WHEN event_date IS NULL OR trim(event_date) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(event_date, 'T') > 0 THEN substr(event_date,1,instr(event_date,'T')-1)
    ELSE event_date
  END AS event_date_only
FROM event
accepted.description: Normalized event rows with parsed ISO datetime parts where possible. Use to join event attributes or filter by date components. Preserves original event columns and exposes derived event_epoch and event_date_only for temporal queries. | Use for: List events by date or date range; Join events to attendance or budgets; Filter events by status or type; Compute time-between-events or ordering

accepted.name: member_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  member_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  email,
  position,
  t_shirt_size,
  phone,
  zip,
  link_to_major,
  -- canonical full name useful for reporting
  trim(COALESCE(first_name,'') || CASE WHEN first_name IS NOT NULL AND last_name IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(last_name,'')) AS full_name
FROM member
accepted.description: Cleaned member rows with canonical full_name and preserved foreign keys to major and zip_code. Use as the starting point for member-level joins and aggregations. | Use for: Member contact lists; Join members to attendance/income/expense/budget; Filter members by position or t_shirt_size

accepted.name: attendance_with_member_event
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.link_to_event,
  a.link_to_member,
  m.member_id AS member_id,
  m.first_name AS first_name,
  m.last_name AS last_name,
  m.email AS email,
  m.position AS position,
  m.t_shirt_size AS t_shirt_size,
  m.phone AS phone,
  m.zip AS zip,
  m.link_to_major AS link_to_major,
  trim(COALESCE(m.first_name,'') || CASE WHEN m.first_name IS NOT NULL AND m.last_name IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(m.last_name,'')) AS full_name,
  e.event_id AS event_id,
  e.event_name AS event_name,
  e.event_date AS event_date,
  e.type AS type,
  e.location AS location,
  e.status AS status
FROM attendance a
LEFT JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id
LEFT JOIN event e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id
accepted.description: One row per attendance linking a member to an event, enriched with member full name and key event attributes. Use for attendance counts, attendee lists, and joining member demographics to events. | Use for: Count attendees per event; List attendees for a given event; Analyze member attendance patterns by major or zip

accepted.name: budget_by_event
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  link_to_event,
  category,
  SUM(COALESCE(spent,0.0)) AS spent,
  SUM(COALESCE(remaining,0.0)) AS remaining,
  SUM(COALESCE(amount,0)) AS amount,
  COUNT(budget_id) AS budget_items
FROM budget
GROUP BY link_to_event, category
accepted.description: Aggregated budget measures per event and category. One row per (link_to_event, category) with sums of spent, remaining, and amount. Useful for event-level budget rollups and comparing categories across events. | Use for: Total spent per event; Budget remaining by event or category; Compare planned amount vs spent by event

accepted.name: expense_by_member
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  link_to_member,
  SUM(COALESCE(cost,0.0)) AS total_cost,
  COUNT(expense_id) AS expense_count,
  MIN(expense_date) AS first_expense_date,
  MAX(expense_date) AS last_expense_date
FROM expense
GROUP BY link_to_member
accepted.description: Per-member expense totals and counts. One row per link_to_member with sum of cost, earliest/latest expense_date, and number of expense transactions. Useful for reimbursements and member spending analysis. | Use for: Sum expenses by member; Identify high spenders (use downstream RANK filter); List members with no expenses by anti-joining

accepted.name: income_by_member
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  link_to_member,
  SUM(COALESCE(amount,0)) AS total_amount,
  COUNT(income_id) AS income_count,
  MIN(date_received) AS first_received_date,
  MAX(date_received) AS last_received_date
FROM income
GROUP BY link_to_member
accepted.description: Per-member income totals and counts. One row per link_to_member with sum of amount, earliest/latest received date, and number of receipts. Useful for dues reporting and member payment tracking. | Use for: Total dues received by member; Identify members with no payments; Trend income by member cohorts

accepted.name: member_demographics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.member_id,
  m.first_name,
  m.last_name,
  m.email,
  m.position,
  m.t_shirt_size,
  m.phone,
  m.zip,
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.type AS type,
  z.city AS city,
  z.county AS county,
  z.state AS state,
  z.short_state AS short_state,
  m.link_to_major,
  ma.major_id AS major_id,
  ma.major_name AS major_name,
  ma.department AS department,
  ma.college AS college
FROM member m
LEFT JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code
LEFT JOIN major ma ON m.link_to_major = ma.major_id
accepted.description: Member rows enriched with major and zip_code descriptive attributes. One row per member preserving link_to_major and zip key columns. Use for demographic breakdowns of members in analyses. | Use for: Break down attendance or finances by major or geography; Export member demographic lists; Filter members by county/state or major

accepted.name: event_financials
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.event_id,
  e.event_name,
  e.event_date,
  e.type,
  e.location,
  e.status,
  COALESCE(bagg.amount,0) AS budgeted_amount,
  COALESCE(bagg.spent,0.0) AS budget_spent,
  COALESCE(bagg.remaining,0.0) AS budget_remaining,
  COALESCE(expagg.expense_cost,0.0) AS expense_cost,
  COALESCE(expagg.expense_count,0) AS expense_count
FROM event e
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT link_to_event, SUM(COALESCE(amount,0)) AS amount, SUM(COALESCE(spent,0.0)) AS spent, SUM(COALESCE(remaining,0.0)) AS remaining
  FROM budget
  GROUP BY link_to_event
) bagg ON e.event_id = bagg.link_to_event
LEFT JOIN (
  -- expenses may link to budgets which link to events; aggregate expenses per event via that path
  SELECT b.link_to_event AS link_to_event, SUM(COALESCE(ex.cost,0.0)) AS expense_cost, COUNT(ex.expense_id) AS expense_count
  FROM expense ex
  LEFT JOIN budget b ON ex.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
  GROUP BY b.link_to_event
) expagg ON e.event_id = expagg.link_to_event
accepted.description: Event-level financial summary joining budgets, expenses, and (optionally) income via members. One row per event_id and aggregates of budgeted amount and spent/remaining from budgets; expenses aggregated by linked budgets that point to the event. Use as starting point for event profitability and reconciliation. | Use for: Compute net expense vs budget per event; List events with expenses but no budget or vice versa; Rank events by overspend or total cost

accepted.name: member_expense_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  link_to_member,
  total_cost,
  expense_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_cost DESC) AS expense_rank
FROM (
  SELECT link_to_member, SUM(COALESCE(cost,0.0)) AS total_cost, COUNT(expense_id) AS expense_count
  FROM expense
  GROUP BY link_to_member
) sub
accepted.description: Per-member ranking by total expense cost using window functions. One row per member with total_cost and rank (1 = highest spender). Downstream queries can filter WHERE rank <= K to get top-K spenders. | Use for: Top K spenders (filter by expense_rank); Rank members by expenses for awards or audits

accepted.name: event_attendance_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.link_to_event,
  COUNT( DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendee_count
FROM attendance a
GROUP BY a.link_to_event
accepted.description: Counts of distinct attendees per event and listable attendee rows. One row per event_id with attendee_count and earliest/latest attendance inferred via member join if needed. | Use for: Attendance per event; Events ordered by attendance (join to event and use ORDER BY attendee_count DESC); Identify events with zero attendance by anti-join
